Look and feel

  • Themes

Themes

mnnn theme list
mnnn theme show
mnnn theme set <NAME>
mnnn theme mode <light|dark|system>
mnnn theme export <NAME> --out FILE
mnnn theme import FILE
mnnn theme reset <NAME>

Built-in themes

Each has a dark and a light variant, with palettes from the published theme specs:

theme dark light
tokyo-night (default) Tokyo Night (Night) Tokyo Night Day
catppuccin Mocha Latte
gruvbox Gruvbox Dark Gruvbox Light
dracula Dracula Alucard
nord Nord (Polar Night) Nord Light (Snow Storm base)
one One Dark One Light
solarized Solarized Dark Solarized Light

Built-ins are compiled in and written to ~/.muninn/themes/<name>/ on first use. Edit them there, or mnnn theme reset <name> to get the shipped version back.

Modes

  • light / dark: use that variant.
  • system: ask the terminal for its background color (OSC 11; luminance < 0.5 means dark), then the OS preference (freedesktop portal org.freedesktop.appearance color-scheme on Linux, AppleInterfaceStyle on macOS, AppsUseLightTheme on Windows), else dark. Re-checked when the terminal regains focus.
  • --theme-mode / MUNINN_THEME_MODE override the mode for one run.

Defaults in preferences: name = "tokyo-night", mode = "system".

interface.toml

[meta]
name = "my-theme"          # folder name: letters, digits, - and _
display_name = "My Theme"
author = "me"
base = "Tokyo Night"

[dark]
variant_name = "My Theme Dark"
bg = "bg"                  # a palette name ...
fg = "#c0caf5"             # ... or a literal #rrggbb
# every role below is required
muted = "comment"
# border, border_focus, selection_bg, selection_fg, accent, header, up, down,
# warning, error, success, info, chart_1 .. chart_6

[dark.palette]
bg = "#1a1b26"
comment = "#565f89"

[light]
# same roles

[light.palette]

Roles: bg, fg, muted, border, border_focus, selection_bg, selection_fg, accent, header, up (bull candle), down (bear candle), warning, error, success, info, chart_1 ... chart_6. A theme missing [dark] or [light], a role, or with a value that is neither #rrggbb nor a palette name fails validation; the TUI then falls back to the default theme and says why. assets/ next to the file is free for your own extras.

Terminals without truecolor get the nearest 256-colour (or 16-colour) approximation, based on COLORTERM and TERM.

Selector (TUI, screen 5)

↑/↓ choose a theme; the right side previews the navigator, a bar table and candles in both variants side by side. Enter applies it, m cycles the mode (system → dark → light), e opens the editor, R resets a built-in.

Editor

↑/↓ pick a role, ←/→ cycle through the theme's palette, Enter types a hex value, v switches between the dark and light variant, g generates a starting variant from the other one, s saves as a new theme, R resets to the base, Esc leaves. The preview updates live and a warning appears when fg/bg, selection or header contrast drops below 4.5:1 (WCAG AA). Solarized Light's published body text is 4.13:1, so it shows that warning by design.

Themes are part of every backup (backup and recovery).
